subject.title: MEDIA: directive with absolute local paths outside default media roots silently fails (Telegram)

question: Should this issue be scoped to dropped-media diagnostics while https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/47002 owns configurable host roots, or should this issue also authorize a new reply-media root configuration surface?
rationale: The diagnostics fix is narrow, but allowing additional host paths changes the local file-read/upload boundary and overlaps an open product/security decision.

options.title: Diagnostics here, roots elsewhere
options.body: Add reasoned warn-level logging and keep the existing generic visible warning here, while routing configurable roots to the related policy issue.

options.title: Define root policy here
options.body: Use this issue to choose and implement a public host-media root contract across schema, docs, and delivery.

options.title: Keep documented behavior only
options.body: Decline new diagnostics/configuration and require users to use managed roots or message-tool sends.

recommendation.title: Diagnostics here, roots elsewhere
recommendation.body: Add reasoned warn-level logging and keep the existing generic visible warning here, while routing configurable roots to the related policy issue.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest recent source-history connection to the outbound media policy and root-plumbing path.
